sentences.text: (Dated this the 3rd day of December, 2025)
The petitioners are the accused persons 2 and 4 in Crime No.25 of 2022 of Karukachal Police Station which is pending as S.C No.275 of 2023 on the file of Fast Track Special Court, Changanassery.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 109, 114, 376, 377 and 506(i) of IPC.

2. The prosecution case is that the first accused being the husband of the de facto complainant with an intention to satisfy his sexual lust and also for unjust enrichment persuaded, the de facto complainant had sexual intercourse with accused persons 2 to 5, received consideration from them,
by compelling and threatening the de facto complainant and thereby they are alleged to have committed the aforesaid offences.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, even as per the allegations raised against the petitioners, no offence as alleged by prosecution is made out and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.
4. The petition was vehemently opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. On a perusal of the FI statement, it is revealed that at 2025:KER:93725 the instigation of the 1st accused, the de facto complainant permitted the other accused persons to have sexual intercourse with her.
From the FI statement, it is also revealed that the 1 st accused had received consideration for the same from the other accused persons.

In the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant, it is stated that no amount of force was used by the petitioners herein for sexually abusing her and also that, she had conceded to the demand of the 1st accused and therefore, in the affidavit, she also prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.
6. At the time of arguments, it is revealed that the de facto complaint as well as the 1 st accused are no more.

On a perusal of the FI statement as well as the affidavit filed by the de facto complainant, it can be seen that the relationship between the de facto complainant and the petitioner was a consensual one and that too for consideration and, as such the offence alleged against the petitioners are not made out.
Moreover, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioners.

State of Karnataka [2015 (7) SCC 423] in which the Apex Court held that "Where, in the opinion of the Court, the chances of ultimate 2025:KER:93725 conviction is bleak and no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution to continue, the Court may quash the proceeding even though it may be at a preliminary stage".
8.

sentences.text: Even otherwise, further proceedings against the petitioners will not yield any result, in the light of the fact that the de facto complainant is no more.
On that ground also there is also no meaning in proceeding further against the petitioners.
9. In the light of the above discussions, I find that this Crl.M.C is liable to be allowed.
In the result, this Crl.M.C allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.C No.275 of 2023 on the file of Fast Track Special Court, Changanassery, arising from Crime No.25 of 2022 of Karukachal Police Station, is quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
